title: Connect biology ideas clearly
objective: Choose a linking word that matches the relationship between ideas.

slides.title: Choose the relationship first
body: Use while to compare. Use however to introduce a contrast or limit.
Use therefore for a conclusion supported by the earlier sentence.

slides.title: Build a careful paragraph
body: “The garden had 6 bees, while the yard had 2. However, we only visited once. We therefore plan another visit.”
First find the comparison. Then find the limit. What action follows from that limit?

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Notes: The first pond had 8 frogs. The second had 3. We counted on one day. We need more visits.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Join the first two ideas with “while”.
Join the last two ideas with “because”.
Use while to compare two places.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Notes: The first tree had 7 birds. The second had 2. We counted on one day. We need more visits.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Join the first two ideas with “while”.
Join the last two ideas with “because”.
Write a short paragraph using your two sentences. Check that both ideas connect clearly.

slides.title: Try removing the linking word
body: Read your paragraph without a link. Ask a partner which relationship is missing. Put back a word that expresses it.
